title: About
content:
The Advocate is the long-running student newspaper of the Graduate Center.

Please see our ‘Contribute!’ page for information about submitting work.

Please see our archives to get a sense of what the Advocate has been up to all these years.

title: Contribute!
content:
The Advocate accepts contributions in the form of articles, reviews, illustrations, and photos from freelance writers, artists, and photographers who are CUNY students, faculty, and staff. The Advocate also accepts contributions from freelance writers, artists, and photographers not affiliated with CUNY. Submit all queries and contributions to our Editor-in-Chief, Dana Burns, at dburns@gradcenter.cuny.edu. Pitches and completed works are welcome.

Payment varies according to how long and/or involved a piece is. Payment for written work usually starts at $100 and caps at $300. Contributors are welcome to send articles on a wide range of topics, including:

  • Investigative articles covering GC/CUNY issues and beyond
  • First-person essays
  • Feature articles on the politics, culture, and art
  • Nontechnical articles on science and technology
  • Provocative or polemical essays on international, national, and local issues
  • Interviews and transcribed discussions or debates
  • Book, film, theater, music, and art reviews

We also accept and pay for creative work! 

The Advocate is always looking for visual art to accompany our articles. We also gladly accept:

  • Creative fiction and nonfiction
  • Experimental and multimedia pieces
  • Poetry
  • Comics

If you would like to submit something that you don’t see mentioned here, please email Dana Burns, at dburns@gradcenter.cuny.edu

Letters to the Editor

We accept but do not pay for letters to the editor.

 

A Note about Editorial Process and Payment

All nonfiction and prose works are edited for clarity and style by our Managing Editor, Coco Fitterman. Creative works are welcome to receive editorial feedback if requested.

Articles are posted online once edited. Articles are usually up on the website 2-4 weeks before they appear in print. As per DGSC rules, payment can only be processed after a piece appears in print. The bureaucratic churn of CUNY will likely further delay your payment. Therefore, while you will be paid for your work, it will likely take a while. EIC will contact you directly if there are any issues with your payment.

 

Wondering if you should Contribute?

The Advocate is a student newspaper based in the Graduate Center, CUNY, but we are happy to feature work on a variety of topics. Our intention is to provide a platform for CUNY students to share their writing, thinking, artwork, or just to sound off. The Advocate is a great place to address CUNY and GC related issues, but also as a jumping-off point for a freelance writing, practice with the editorial process, or a place to workshop ideas and research. If you’d like to write for the Advocate but don’t know where to start, send us a pitch or shoot us an email detailing your interests and areas of expertise. We might be able to pass along an assignment!

Finally, the Advocate used to have an exhaustive list of editorial guidelines grandfathered in from past iterations. Please disregard for future contributions.

 

Thanks!
